Subject: RE: Request: GTM/container & consent banner evidence for upcoming procurement

Hi Mark / Lydia — Naomi here from Privacy Ops. Answers inline below and I’ve pasted links to our internal SOPs.

1) Consent gating: Yes. All marketing pixels and non-essential tags are configured to run only when the visitor has given marketing/analytics consent. The GTM container uses a consent check dataLayer variable and ConsentFlow CMP integration — when consent is denied the associated tags do not fire. We have a verified test plan that exercises reject/allow flows.

2) Consent logs: ConsentFlow stores consent records in our EU tenant in encrypted form. Retention is configurable; our default retention is 13 months for cookie consent logs. We can provide export of consent events for the last 12 months upon written request (see attached export process doc link).

3) Revocation: Users can revoke consent via the Manage vendors link on the banner, which updates the ConsentFlow state and writes a new consent event. Tags will stop firing on subsequent page loads. We also have a client-side runtime check that evaluates consent before tag execution to prevent in-session firing when consent is removed.

Contract language: We can provide the following clause for inclusion in the DPA or SOW: 

"Redwood confirms that (i) marketing and analytics tags are disabled for EU/EEA visitors who do not provide marketing consent; (ii) consent events are logged and stored in encrypted form in our EU tenant; and (iii) customers may request consent log exports for audit within the standard retention period."

If that works for Legal, Karthik — feel free to paste it into the contract redline. I’ve also attached: a short SOP excerpt URL and a link to the consent export runbook.

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Privacy Operations Manager, Redwood Inference
